domain_setting: An everyday digital-device ecosystem, from portable electronics and computer equipment to online services and common device actions.
global_art_direction: Use contemporary but brand-free electronic objects with strong silhouettes, clean device screens, and a calm editorial studio finish.
Keep screens blank or filled only with geometric image blocks, abstract lines, and pictograms; use no letters, numbers, logos, brand marks, or readable interface text.

Distinguish adjacent hardware carefully: pocket GPS versus dashboard satnav; keyboard versus musical keys; computer versus tower-based desktop computer; power cord versus charging adapter; smartphone versus broad tablet; mouse pad versus computer mouse.
Show software and online concepts through device context and physical relationships rather than floating generic symbols alone.
Use volumetric forms, real-thickness cables, clipped shading, compact details, and comfortable thumbnail scale; do not draw stick people or thin single-line limbs.
Keep every essential contour inside the safe zone and use the same Artico ink and layered five-group source structure.

same_term_course_art_reviewed.reason: The existing automotive battery and jumper leads fit vehicle repair, while this gadgets chapter needs portable rechargeable cells.
The existing handheld GPS receiver is an unambiguous navigation gadget and suits this device group.
The scene centers a person and an industrial machine, not technology as a broad digital-device concept.
The factory worker scene is industrial and too specific for the lesson general digital technology sense.
The existing illustration shows a manager leading coworkers, the wrong sense.
The envelope on a computer screen clearly depicts electronic mail.
A large padlock protecting a digital account clearly depicts a password.
A document being discarded in a wastebasket clearly shows the device action.

reviewed_existing_art.reason: No artwork was mapped to Lesson 76. Exact-term illustrations from earlier lessons were reviewed; four clear digital/device scenes are reused, while vehicle-specific, industrial, and wrong-sense art is replaced.

entries.battery: A compact rechargeable battery pack and two loose cells, with a charging cradle to establish it as power for small electronics rather than a car battery.
entries.bulb: A smart light bulb with a rounded glass envelope, visible spiral filament, metal screw base, and a gentle connected glow.
entries.camera: A digital mirrorless camera with a prominent lens, shutter button, textured grip, and a small rear preview screen showing a landscape.
entries.computer: An all-in-one desktop computer with one broad monitor, keyboard, and mouse; keep its tower out of view so it differs from the full desktop setup.
entries.desktop computer: A desktop computer setup with a separate monitor, upright tower case, keyboard, mouse, and visible ventilation slots.
entries.e-reader: A thin e-reader held open beside a closed paper book, showing a page-like screen with simple non-letter line marks.
entries.earphones: Two in-ear buds with soft silicone tips joined by a thin connecting cord and a small control capsule.
entries.gadgets: A tidy group of small everyday electronic devices: smartwatch, compact camera, earphones, and a handheld game controller.
entries.gps: A compact handheld GPS receiver with a small map-like screen and satellite cues; reuse the clear portable navigation receiver from Lesson 46.
entries.laptop: An open portable laptop with a slim hinged screen, keyboard, trackpad, and visible side ports.
entries.satnav: A dashboard-mounted satellite navigation screen with a route line and a vehicle windshield behind it; distinguish it from a pocket GPS receiver.
entries.screen: A standalone flat digital display panel viewed at a slight angle, with a glowing color field and bezel; depict electronic screen, not mesh.
entries.smartphone: A modern touch-screen phone with camera lenses, side buttons, and an abstract home-screen grid without lettering.
entries.smartwatch: A wristwatch with a touch display, short strap, sensor dots, and a wrist to show that it is worn.
entries.tablet (gadget): A thin handheld tablet computer with a broad touch screen and rear camera, unmistakably electronic rather than a stone tablet.
entries.technology: A contemporary computing workstation with circuit board, monitor, and connected devices, expressing applied digital technology without a person or factory.
entries.computer desk: A compact study desk supporting monitor, keyboard, mouse, lamp, and neatly managed cables.
entries.hard drive: A computer hard-drive enclosure opened enough to reveal a silver platter and read arm, beside its outer casing.
entries.keyboard: A computer keyboard in close view with keycaps, space bar, and a coiled connection lead; no musical context.
entries.power cord: A thick detachable power cord ending in a two-prong wall plug, with insulated cable loops.
entries.lead (electrical): An insulated electrical lead joining a device plug to a power source; keep it visibly a cable, not a person guiding someone.
entries.memory card: A small SD-style memory card with gold contact strip and a camera slot for scale.
entries.mouse (computer): A computer mouse with scroll wheel, two buttons, curved shell, and cable; no animal context.
entries.mouse pad / mouse mat (often uk): A rectangular fabric mouse mat with stitched edges and a computer mouse gliding on its surface.
entries.usb drive: A compact flash drive with a metal USB connector and protective cap beside a computer port.
entries.charger: A wall charger block with folded prongs and a cable connected to a phone, showing power transfer rather than a person charging.
entries.app: A phone screen organized into a grid of distinct simple pictograms that represent a software application menu; no letters.
entries.browser: A monitor displaying a framed webpage layout with a top toolbar, tabs, and image blocks but no words or symbols.
entries.email: A digital message represented by a computer screen and a sealed envelope motif; reuse the clear existing envelope card from Lesson 7.
entries.login: A person approaching a computer account through a secure doorway motif: user silhouette and a key entering a lock beside the screen.
entries.password: A secure padlock protecting a device screen; reuse the clear lock illustration from Lesson 7.
entries.router: A wireless router with two antennae, Ethernet ports, and radiating Wi-Fi arcs connecting nearby devices.
entries.text: A smartphone receiving a short text message, conveyed by paired blank message bubbles and a notification pulse; no lettering.
entries.website: A desktop monitor showing a layered website layout with navigation bar, image blocks, and a page footer, all unlabeled.
entries.wi-fi: A router connecting a phone, laptop, and tablet through clear concentric signal arcs.
entries.back up: A laptop and external drive connected as a duplicate set of files moves from the computer toward the storage drive.
entries.click: A fingertip pressing a computer mouse button with a short tactile click burst and pointer movement.
entries.delete: A document card being removed into a wastebasket; reuse the clear delete illustration from Lesson 7.
entries.download: A file represented by a blank page descends from a cloud into an open laptop.
entries.log in: A user silhouette passes through an open secure doorway into a computer account, keyed by a lock and device.
entries.log out: A user silhouette leaves a lit computer session through an outward doorway cue, clearly opposite logging in.
entries.plug in: A two-prong electrical plug enters a wall socket, with the cable leading toward a device.
entries.turn off: A hand moves a device switch to its off position as the display and indicator light go dark.
entries.turn on: A hand presses a power button as the device display illuminates and a small indicator light glows.
entries.update: A phone receives a refreshed software screen, shown by circular arrows around the device and a changed panel layout without text.
entries.upload: A blank file rises from a laptop toward a cloud, carried by a clear upward arrow.
